chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Abdullah Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the inheritance of the newborn from the wergild, he (peace be upon him) said: 'He does not inherit anything from the wergild until he shrieks and his voice is heard.'

key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: Blood money or compensation paid for death or injury
key_terms.الْمَنفُوسُ: A newborn infant who has been separated from the womb
key_terms.يَصِيحَ: To shriek or cry out loudly, indicating distinct life

ai.seo_question: When does a newborn inherit blood money from their mother's death?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that a newborn is not entitled to inherit the mother's blood money (diyah) unless they exhibit clear signs of life, specifically by crying audibly. This criterion distinguishes mere birth from viable life, ensuring that inheritance rights are only triggered when the infant demonstrates independent existence, a principle deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence regarding the timing of legal personality.
